text:
alex_cs: FYI customer (AcadiaHealth) opened a ticket — embeddings endpoints started returning 403s ~2h ago. Generation/chat still works. Request id: req_0b3c9f. They rolled a deploy yesterday but say nothing changed in their client.

sam_support: Oof. Any quick repro steps or example curl?

alex_cs: Pasted example from the customer (sanitized) — they do a normal bearer auth call to /v1/embeddings. Works sometimes, fails other times.

alex_cs: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-svc-xxxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"open-embed-1","input":"foo"}'
```

maria_engineering: Can you grab the token header/claims for one failing request (decoded JWT)? Looks like an entitlement/scope mismatch from the error pattern you pasted earlier.

alex_cs: Got one from debug logs. Token claims look weird: scope string has URL-encoded pluses instead of spaces. Copying below.

alex_cs: ```json
{"iss":"auth.redwood.internal","sub":"svcacct:acadia","scope":"embeddings+generation+rerank","exp":1745871490}
```

sam_support: Ahhh. The scope separator should be a space char per RFC — our provisioner expects spaces, but we've historically tolerated '+' from some legacy clients. If the token parser is strict it will not match "embeddings" scope and reject.

devops_bot: [alert] ingress-proxy/1.12.0 rolled at 2025-06-25T01:20Z — default header normalization switched to `+`->`%20` preservation mode. See changelog: https://internal.ops/ingress/changeset/1.12.0

maria_engineering: That explains it. The provisioner-proxy used to normalize `+` to space on decode; new proxy preserves `+` literally so our JWT claims string ends up with plus signs. Our scope parser does a space-split so nothing matches.

maria_engineering: Short-term fix: treat `+` as space in the scope parser and accept both. I'll open a tiny patch. Long-term: normalize at the auth edge or have provisioner produce proper space-separated scopes.

provisioner-bot: Note: provisioner v2.3.1 still emits space-separated scopes, but some older service-keys created by internal scripts used URL-encoded scopes (using `+`) when saving. We have a migration task pending.

alex_cs: Customer asks for workaround while you patch — can we advise them to rotate the key or a temp policy? They want minimal disruption.

maria_engineering: Two options: 1) Rotate to a freshly provisioned svc key (preferred) — new keys will have proper spaces. 2) We can enable tolerant parsing (server-side) and release within a few hours; rollback ingress normalization if needed. Which is faster for ops?

devops_bot: Rolling back ingress change requires approval but is doable. Enabling tolerant parsing is a single-line change in auth library and can be deployed to prod in a canary within ~45 minutes.

sam_support: I'll offer the customer the rotate-key workaround first (lowest blast radius) and say we're doing a server fix. They accepted key rotation for now but asked for a timeline on the server change.

maria_engineering: I'll PR the tolerant-scope-parser patch now, add unit tests for "embeddings+generation" and "embeddings generation", and request a fasttrack review. If CI is clean I can merge and push canary by EOD.

alex_cs: Thanks — please @sam_support when the canary is live so I can tell Acadia. Also please add a short explainer we can forward to their security team about why rotation fixes it immediately.

maria_engineering: Will do. Also adding a note to the provisioner migration task to clean up keys created pre-2024 that may have encoded scopes.

alex_cs: Great. Customer is satisfied with rotation + patch timeline. Marking the internal ticket as high-priority follow-up. :thumbsup:

provisioner-bot: follow-up task created: PROV-1428 "migrate legacy svc-keys with encoded scope separators"
